rationale: T_eff = 0.2*target + d fits exactly, so at the 0.45 frac floor only IO-path delay d (~3.71 ns) can fall. ABC sizing and slew/cap margins moved d by <=6 ps (inert at +5.6 ns slack); placement is the big lever (timing-driven runs 1.3-2 ns better), and orfs RC beat stock/cap213 within both TD and non-TD groups, so keep it. Least-explored lever: placement density. Bracket it from the best run (DELAY 4, 40/40, orfs, TD): (1) spread, util 20 + density 27% (aes's good run used 30%) so IO-path cells sit nearer their pins; (2) compact, density 51%, for shorter critical wires and a smaller clock tree.
